summary: Kiribati's Entry and Visa Exemption Order 2023 waives the requirement to hold a visa permitting travel to Kiribati for citizens of the countries and regions on its list, which includes the United Kingdom, the United States of America, China and Japan; the maximum stay under the exemption must not exceed 90 days in any 12-month period. Kiribati's Immigration Procedures say a non-citizen may travel to Kiribati only as the holder of a visa or as a person to whom a visa waiver applies. The exemption order requires a passport valid for not less than six months on the day of departure from Kiribati, and the UK government says you must hold a ticket for return or onward travel and enough funds for your stay.

tips.text: The UK government says very few places accept credit cards in Kiribati, and that there are ATMs at branches of the Bank of Kiribati and ANZ in Betio, Bairiki and Bikenibeu on Tarawa atoll.

The UK government says medical facilities at the general hospital in Tarawa are modest, that prescription and non-prescription medicines are generally not available so you should bring any medicines you need with you, and that if you need any non-basic medical treatment you will usually need medical evacuation, so you should have adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds to cover evacuation by air ambulance.

Canada's travel advice says the rainy seasons in the South Pacific extend from November to April, and that severe rainstorms can cause flooding and landslides, which can hamper overland, maritime and air travel.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Kiribati?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Kiribati's Entry and Visa Exemption Order 2023 waives the requirement to hold a visa permitting travel to Kiribati for citizens of the countries and regions on its list, which includes the United Kingdom, the United States of America, China and Japan; the maximum stay under the exemption must not exceed 90 days in any 12-month period. Kiribati's Immigration Procedures say a non-citizen may travel to Kiribati only as the holder of a visa or as a person to whom a visa waiver applies.

faq.question: How do I get a visitor visa if my country is not exempt?
faq.answer: Kiribati's Immigration Procedures say a non-citizen may travel to Kiribati only as the holder of a visa or as a person to whom a visa waiver applies. To be granted a visitor visa, applicants must meet the generic temporary entry requirements for lodging an application, bona fide applicants, and health and character; meet the funds or sponsorship requirements; meet the onward travel requirements, if relevant; and be coming to Kiribati for a lawful purpose. The Procedures say a paper application is lodged on the date it is received at the Immigration office. No official source we could read describes how to apply from abroad.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Kiribati?
faq.answer: Kiribati's Entry and Visa Exemption Order 2023 says the maximum stay under the exemption must not exceed 90 days in any given 12-month period. The UK government says British citizens can visit Kiribati without a visa for up to one month, that the authorities will normally grant a one-month stay on arrival, and that you can apply for one-month extensions, up to a maximum of 3 extra months, from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration in Bairiki.

faq.question: Is travel insurance required for Kiribati?
faq.answer: No official source we could read makes travel insurance a condition of entry. The UK government says that if you need any non-basic medical treatment you will usually need medical evacuation from Kiribati, and to make sure you have adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds to cover evacuation by air ambulance plus the cost of medical treatment abroad and repatriation.

faq.question: Can I use cards or ATMs in Kiribati?
faq.answer: The UK government says very few places accept credit cards in Kiribati, and that there are ATMs at branches of the Bank of Kiribati and ANZ in Betio, Bairiki and Bikenibeu on Tarawa atoll. Canada's travel advice says the currency is the Australian dollar, that there are a limited number of ATMs and that Visa and MasterCard are accepted at most hotels.
